So the idea is that the final product enables CDN peering, meaning distinct CDNs internetwork and deliver content in a coordinated, cooperative way. That lets providers rapidly scale out to handle both flash crowds and anticipated increases in demand, and it removes the need for any single CDN to provision all the resources itself. Now, whether the peering is ad-hoc or planned, it needs fundamental research on the core problems: measuring and disseminating load information, doing request assignment and redirection, enabling content replication, and working out appropriate compensation among the participants, all at a geographically distributed, Internet scale. In a single CDN those issues are deeply interrelated and co-dependent. Here the main thrust is to handle them in a coordinated and cooperative manner across many peered CDNs, while still satisfying the complex multi-dimensional constraints each individual provider has."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Great, thanks.
